extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), corporate secretaries, general counsel, investor_relations and compliance officers preparing proxy statements/annual reports
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and disclosure standards under Regulation S-K Item 407 (and related Items) governing nominating committees, audit and compensation committees, shareholder communications, hedging, and insider trading arrangements for proxy statements and annual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of security-holder recommended nominees (Item 407(c)(2)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the nominating committee received, by a date not later than the 120th calendar day before last year's proxy statement release date, a recommended nominee from a security holder (or group) owning >5% beneficially for at least one year, identify the candidate and the security holder or group that recommended the candidate and disclose whether the nominating committee chose to nominate the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No identification/disclosure required without written consent of both the security holder (or group) and the candidate. See related instructions on ownership proof and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 120-day timing and alternate timing when meeting date changed
rubrics_metrics.description: The 120-calendar-day-before requirement triggers the disclosure obligation for recommended nominees; where the annual meeting date changed by more than 30 days from the prior year, the obligation arises when the registrant receives the recommendation a reasonable time before the registrant begins to print and mail proxy materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 120-day rule as default; adjust for material meeting date shifts (>30 days) to a 'reasonable time' standard tied to printing/mailing schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of security-holder percentage using filed reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of securities held by a recommending security holder may be determined using information in the registrant's most recent quarterly or annual report and any subsequent current report filed under the Exchange Act (or Form N-CSR for certain investment companies), unless the party relying on such report knows or has reason to believe it is inaccurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits reliance on public filings to calculate >5% ownership; registrant must be alert to known inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable evidence of ownership and holding period for non-registered holders
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recommending security holder is not the registered holder, they may submit (a) a written statement from the record holder (broker/bank) verifying continuous one-year holding, or (b) copies of Schedule 13D/13G, Form 3/4/5 (or amendments/updates) reflecting ownership as of or before the recommendation date plus a written statement that holdings were continuous for one year as of the recommendation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registrants clear documentary alternatives to verify both percentage ownership and one-year holding requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written consent and proof at time of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The security holder or group must provide, at the time of the recommendation, the written consent of all parties to be identified and, where members are not registered holders, proof that the group satisfied the required ownership percentage and holding period as of the recommendation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent documents and proof should be contemporaneous with the recommendation; absence of consent prevents identification/disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'nominating committee' for Item 407(c)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'nominating committee' includes nominating committees and committees performing similar functions, as well as groups of directors fulfilling the role (including the entire board).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Item 407(c)(2) requirements to any body performing nominating functions, not just formally-titled committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material changes to shareholder nomination procedures (Item 407(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any material changes to the procedures by which security holders may recommend nominees to the board, where those changes were implemented after the registrant last provided disclosure under Item 407(c)(2)(iv) or (c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclosure need only be provided in quarterly or annual reports. Adoption of procedures where none were previously disclosed constitutes a material change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit committee charter disclosure (Item 407(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the audit committee has a charter. If it has a charter, provide the disclosure required by Instruction 2 regarding the audit committee charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction 2 explains availability on website or inclusion in proxy appendix at least once every three fiscal years or when materially amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure when appointing a non-independent audit committee director
rubrics_metrics.description: If the board determines to appoint to the audit committee a director who is not independent (apart from §240.10A-3 requirements), disclose the nature of the relationship that makes the individual not independent and the reasons for the board's determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required where exceptional or limited circumstances lead to non-independent appointment; explain relationships and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit committee statements on review and recommendation of financial statements (Item 407(d)(3)(i)(A)-(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: The audit committee must state whether it: (A) reviewed and discussed the audited financial statements with management; (B) discussed with independent auditors the matters required by PCAOB and the Commission; (C) received the written disclosures/letter from the independent accountant regarding independence and discussed independence; and (D) based on those reviews recommended to the board that the audited financial statements be included in the annual report or equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All four elements should be addressed in the required disclosure; these are factual statements about committee actions and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of audit committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of each member of the company's audit committee (or, in the absence of an audit committee, the board committee performing equivalent functions or the entire board) must appear below the audit committee disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List committee members immediately following the substantive audit committee statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listed issuer audit committee composition and identification (Item 407(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is a listed issuer filing a Form 10-K or proxy where directors are elected and not relying on certain exemptions, state whether it has a separately-designated standing audit committee established under section 3(a)(58)(A) or a committee performing similar functions and identify each committee member; or state if the entire board is acting as the audit committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provide disclosure required by §240.10A-3(d) regarding exemptions from listing standards, if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit committee financial expert disclosure (Item 407(d)(5)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the board has determined the registrant either (1) has at least one audit committee financial expert serving on its audit committee, or (2) does not have such an expert. If (1), disclose the expert's name and whether that person is independent (as defined by listing standards). If (2), explain why there is no audit committee financial expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names of additional experts may be disclosed but are not required; if disclosed, indicate independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'audit committee financial expert' attributes (Item 407(d)(5)(ii)(A)-(E))
rubrics_metrics.description: An audit committee financial expert is a person with: (A) understanding of GAAP and financial statements; (B) ability to assess application of such principles for estimates/accruals/reserves; (C) experience preparing/auditing/analyzing financial statements with comparable breadth/complexity or supervising such persons; (D) understanding of internal control over financial reporting; and (E) understanding of audit committee functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five attributes define the substantive qualifications expected of the 'financial expert' designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible ways to acquire financial expert attributes (Item 407(d)(5)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may have acquired the audit committee financial expert attributes through: (A) education/experience as a principal financial officer, controller, public accountant/auditor or similar positions; (B) experience actively supervising such persons; (C) experience overseeing or assessing companies or accountants regarding preparation/auditing/evaluation of financial statements; or (D) other relevant experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should provide a brief listing of relevant experience if qualification relies on (D) 'other relevant experience'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for designation of audit committee financial expert (Item 407(d)(5)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation as an audit committee financial expert will not make the person an 'expert' for purposes (including section 11 of the Securities Act), will not impose greater duties/obligations/liability than otherwise as a committee/board member, and will not affect duties/obligations/liability of other members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a disclosure safe harbor limiting legal implications of the label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, filing location, and exemptions for audit committee financial expert disclosure (Instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure under Item 407(d)(5) is required only in a registrant's annual report (need not be in proxy/info statement unless incorporated by reference). Foreign private issuer adjustments exist for board definitions and GAAP. Asset-backed issuers are exempt from this disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Instruction 1-4 for annual-report-only requirement, foreign issuer definitions, and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-soliciting/materiality and frequency instructions for Item 407(d)(1)-(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information required by paragraphs (d)(1)-(3) is not deemed 'soliciting material' or 'filed' with the Commission (subject to exceptions) and will not be incorporated by reference except as registrant specifies. The disclosure need only be provided one time during any fiscal year and need only appear in filings relating to the annual meeting where directors are to be elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains limited filing liability and frequency; registrant control over incorporation by reference matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation committee absence disclosure (Item 407(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant does not have a standing compensation committee or equivalent, state the basis for the board's view that it is appropriate not to have such a committee and identify each director who participates in consideration of executive officer and director compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale and list of participants when no formal committee exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation committee charter disclosure (Item 407(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the compensation committee has a charter. If so, provide the disclosure required by Instruction 2 (availability on website or inclusion in proxy appendix as specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar website/appendix requirements as audit committee charters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative description of processes/procedures for determining executive/director compensation (Item 407(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a narrative description of the registrant's processes and procedures for consideration and determination of executive and director compensation, including: (i) scope of authority of the compensation committee and extent of delegation; (ii) any role of executive officers in determining or recommending compensation; (iii) any role of compensation consultants in determining or recommending compensation (with limits for broad-based plans), identifying consultants, engagement source, nature/scope of assignment and material elements of instructions given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear descriptions of delegation, executive officer influence, and consultant engagement details where consultants advise on compensation amounts/forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation consultant fee disclosure when other services exceed $120,000 (Item 407(e)(3)(iii)(A)-(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a compensation consultant engaged by the committee provided additional services to the registrant or affiliates exceeding $120,000 in the fiscal year, disclose aggregate fees for compensation advice and aggregate fees for other services, and whether management recommended engaging the consultant and whether the committee/board approved such other services. If management (not committee) engaged a consultant and that consultant provided >$120,000 in additional services, disclose aggregate fees for compensation advice and for additional services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose fee amounts and who engaged the consultant to surface potential conflicts or influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of compensation consultant conflicts and addressing methods (Item 407(e)(3)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a compensation consultant's work has raised any conflict of interest, disclose the nature of the conflict and how the conflict is being addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider factors listed in §240.10C-1(b)(4)(i)-(vi) among those relevant to determining conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation disclosures (Item 407(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 'Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation' identify each person who served as a compensation committee member during the last fiscal year and indicate if they were an officer/employee, former officer, or had any relationship requiring disclosure under Item 404; if no committee, identify each officer/employee/former officer who participated in compensation deliberations; describe specified interlock relationships (executive officer serving on another entity's compensation committee where another of that entity's executive officers served on registrant's committee; executive serving as director of other entity where one of that entity's executive officers served on registrant's committee; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompany disclosures about such persons with Item 404 disclosures where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation Committee Report requirements (Item 407(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The compensation committee must state whether it has reviewed and discussed the Compensation Discussion and Analysis (CD&A) with management and whether, based on that review, it recommended to the board that the CD&A be included in the registrant's annual report on Form 10-K, proxy statement on Schedule 14A, or information statement on Schedule 14C. The names of each committee member must appear below this disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This report is factual: whether review/discussion occurred and the committee's recommendation; list member names beneath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareholder communications process disclosure (Item 407(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the board provides a process for security holders to send communications to the board; if not, state the board's basis for not having such a process. If a process exists, describe how security holders can send communications and, if not all communications are sent directly to board members, describe the process for determining which communications will be relayed to board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May provide a website address instead of including the information in the proxy. Process for collection/organization need not be disclosed if approved by majority of independent directors (or non-interested directors for investment companies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and limits relating to security holder communications (Instructions to Item 407(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications from an officer or director of the registrant are not 'security holder communications.' Communications from an employee or agent are security holder communications only if made solely in such person's capacity as a security holder. Security holder proposals under §240.14a-8 and related communications are not 'security holder communications' for this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps registrants classify and decide what to disclose under (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller reporting company and emerging growth company exemptions (Item 407(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant qualifying as a 'smaller reporting company' is not required to provide the audit committee financial expert disclosure in its first annual report after initial registration and is not required to provide certain compensation committee disclosures. An 'emerging growth company' is not required to provide the disclosure required by paragraph (e)(5) (compensation committee report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these exemptions when registrant meets the statutory definitions cited (see §§ 229.10(f)(1), Rule 405 of the Securities Act, Rule 12b-2 of the Exchange Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board leadership structure and role in risk oversight disclosure (Item 407(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe the leadership structure of the board (e.g., whether same person is CEO and chairman or separate) and, if the CEO is also chairman (or chairman is an 'interested person' for investment companies), disclose whether there is a lead independent director and that person's specific role. Explain why the registrant determined the leadership structure is appropriate given its characteristics, and disclose extent of the board's role in risk oversight and effect on leadership structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale tailored to company-specific circumstances and describe how risk oversight is administered by the board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee, officer and director hedging policy disclosure (Item 407(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: In proxy/info statements for director elections, describe any practices or policies regarding the ability of employees (including officers) or directors (or their designees) to purchase financial instruments or engage in transactions that hedge or offset decreases in registrant equity securities (whether granted as compensation or held personally).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a fair and accurate summary of the practices/policies including categories of persons covered, or disclose policies in full. Also describe categories of hedging transactions specifically permitted and specifically disallowed. If no such policies exist, state that fact or that such transactions are generally permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of registrant equity securities and incorporation rule (Instruction to Item 407(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Registrant equity securities' are those defined in section 3(a)(11) of the Exchange Act and §240.3a11-1. Information required by Item 407(i) will not be deemed incorporated by reference into other filings except to the extent registrant specifies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope of the hedging disclosure and incorporation-by-reference rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading arrangements disclosure (Item 408(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether, during the registrant's last fiscal quarter (fourth fiscal quarter for annual report), any director or officer adopted or terminated any Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement or any 'non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a quarter-by-quarter disclosure obligation; see Item 408(c) for definition of non-Rule arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material terms to identify for trading arrangements (Item 408(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the trading arrangement is intended to satisfy the affirmative defense of Rule 10b5-1(c) and provide a description of the material terms (other than price terms), including: (A) the name and title of the director or officer; (B) the date the arrangement was adopted or terminated; (C) the duration of the trading arrangement; and (D) the aggregate number of securities to be purchased or sold pursuant to the arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude price-specific terms from disclosure; include the named elements. The disclosure must be provided in an Interactive Data File per EDGAR requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive Data File requirement for Item 408(a) and (b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure provided under Item 408(a)(1)-(2) and Item 408(b)(1) must be provided in an Interactive Data File as required by 17 CFR 232.405 (EDGAR Filer Manual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must format required disclosures in the specified machine-readable EDGAR interactive data format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading policies and procedures disclosure and exhibit requirement (Item 408(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the registrant has adopted insider trading policies/procedures reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws, rules and listing standards; if not, explain why. If adopted, file such policies/procedures as an exhibit. If all such policies are included in the code of ethics and the code is filed as an exhibit, that satisfies the exhibit requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires the disclosure to be provided in an Interactive Data File per 17 CFR 232.405.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and criteria of a 'non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement' (Item 408(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered person (director/officer) has a non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement where: (1) the covered person asserts that at the time they adopted a written arrangement they were not aware of material nonpublic information, and (2) the trading arrangement either: (i) specified amount/price/date; (ii) included a written formula/algorithm/computer program for determining amount/price/date; or (iii) did not permit the covered person to exercise subsequent influence over how/when/whether trades are effected, provided any other person exercising such influence was not aware of material nonpublic information when doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets objective/formal criteria distinguishing non-Rule arrangements for disclosure purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 501 Forepart and outside front cover page requirements (Subpart 229.500)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant must furnish the specified information in plain English (see §230.421(d) of Regulation C). For the front cover of the registration statement include the delaying amendment legend where appropriate. The outside front cover page of the prospectus must be limited to one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates plain-English presentation and a one-page limit for the outside front cover; follow Regulation C references for formatting language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter availability and appendix inclusion instruction (Instruction to Item 407, paragraph 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For paragraphs (c)(2)(i), (d)(1) and (e)(2), disclose whether a current copy of the applicable committee charter is available to security holders on the registrant's website; if not available online, include a copy of the charter in an appendix to the proxy/information statement at least once every three fiscal years or if materially amended since the beginning of the last fiscal year. If neither online nor included in appendix, identify which prior fiscal years the charter was included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural alternatives to make charters available to security holders and documents historical compliance.
